text:
mike_ops: FYI getting a high-severity customer escalation — hosted API between SFO edge -> eu1 is returning lots of 502s and timeouts. Customer reports failed requests + auth retries.

svc-monitor: Alert: hosted-api-prod 5xx rate spiked 11x at 2026-03-16T18:04Z for route /v1/generate. Link: https://grafana.redwood/hosted/alerts/1234 :rotating_light:

sarah_support: Which customers? any request ids? I have a Support ticket with stack traces. They included curl repro and we can reproduce from their region.

mike_ops: Customer: fintech-app-prod (multi-tenant). Example req id in logs: r-0a1b2c3d. Occurs from SFO region to model eu1-replica. Frequent 502 + occasional 504.

tom_infra: I'm seeing packet loss on the SFO egress interface towards the transit provider for AS64501. Quick mtr from an SFO edge node to eu1-egress:

```
# mtr -r -c 10 eu1-gw.example.net
1. 10.0.8.1 0.0% 1 ms
2. transit-1.isp 0.0% 12 ms
3. transit-2.isp 0.0% 14 ms
4. core-peering.isp 56.0% 120 ms  <-- huge loss here
5. eu1-edge 58.0% 135 ms
```

tom_infra: tcpdump on sfo-egress shows repeated retransmits + ack gaps: `tcp retransmission` and visible RSTs when requests stall.

oncall-bot: Incident ticket #INC-2026-318 created and paged oncall. Priority: Sev2.

ben_prod: Noting we also see a bump in auth-service retries (401 -> retry -> 5xx). Possibly token exchange hits eu1 and gets dropped mid-flight. Need to check auth token service endpoint routing.

elaine_se: Customer provided reproducer: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx" https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'` -> consistent 502s (~3/5 attempts).

sarah_support: Can infra route around the transit peer? Any quick mitigation like BGP community to steer away? Customer is on a paid SLA.

tom_infra: I'm engaging transit provider engineering now. Short-term mitigation: fail traffic to eu1 via alternate peering (eu-direct) — rolling BGP community change on the SFO egress. Applying in 60s. Will monitor.

svc-monitor: After BGP adjust: 5xx rate dropped to 2.3x baseline, latency p50 improved. Still seeing occasional 502s from the older sessions due to TCP keepalive reset.

mike_ops: Good — keep the customer updated. Sarah, tell them we applied a routing change and are monitoring. Ask them to retry and share new request ids if persists.

sarah_support: Messaged customer: "We’ve applied a temporary routing change away from the degraded transit peer. Please retry and send any failing request ids. We’ll keep you posted." :thumbsup:

ben_prod: Follow-up action items: 1) capture full tcpdump + pcap for the incident and attach to INC ticket. 2) run packet captures at eu1 to confirm symmetric loss. 3) add automatic reroute policy for persistent packetloss > 20% for 3m.

tom_infra: PCAP uploaded to ticket (link). Transit confirmed microbursting on their core link between POP-7 and POP-8. They plan hardware swap. ETA ~2h.

elaine_se: Customer replied: retry attempts are much better now, saw near-zero 502s after 10:20Z. They asked for a post-mortem and credits per SLA.

mike_ops: Marking this as mitigated. Will keep open until transit fix complete and we’ve validated 24h stability.

sarah_support: Closing the support escalation with the customer and creating credit request per SLA.

oncall-bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> monitoring. INC-2026-318 assigned to tom_infra.

ben_prod: Note for the postmortem: consider adding health-check-based ephemeral BGP community automation, and check auth token service retry idempotency to avoid double-charge or billing anomalies.

mike_ops: Thanks all — please drop any additional logs to INC-2026-318.
